sources.summary: South Norfolk Council's notice under Article 15 of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015 lists applications submitted to the council, among them 2026/2957, KESWICK AND INTWOOD, Land West of Ipswich Road, Keswick: construction of a data centre (Use Class B8) including ancillary office accommodation, associated infrastructure, substations, backup generators, access, parking, landscaping, sustainable drainage systems and associated works, advertised as a major development (and for its effect on a listed building or its curtilage). Comments are invited within 21 days; the notice records no decision. The same notice reports an unrelated Regulation 30 decision on an Orsted energy-balancing scheme at Swardeston.
sources.date_semantics: The notice is dated 15 October 2026 and the portal shows it as published on 15/10/26 in the Eastern Daily Press. Used as a 15 October 2026 announcement observation of the data-centre application. It is an application notice, not a decision: no consent and no physical work are implied. The signing officer's name and the newspaper's contact details are not reproduced.

sources.title: Environment Agency Compliance Assessment Report VP3225SC/0605191: site inspection and liaison at Vantage LHR21, 37-39 North Acton Road (permit EPR/VP3225SC, VDC LHR21 Limited), 11 August 2026, issued 17 August 2026
sources.publisher: Environment Agency (Public Registers Online, installations compliance documents)
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (Environment Agency conditional licence as stated in the register metadata)
sources.summary: Six-page EPR Compliance Assessment Report for site 'Vantage LHR21', permit VP3225SC, operator/permit holder VDC LHR21 Limited: site inspection and liaison on 11 August 2026 (10:00-14:15), date issued 17 August 2026, no breaches (band A). The officer records that the meeting, with Vantage's environmental permitting manager, the LHR21 operations manager and project manager and two consultancies, was 'for the commissioning of the site which was still under construction'. Items inspected included an external engine ready for craning, engine containers and empty bays, fuel fill point and leak detection, some fuel pipework under construction and blanked off, stacks, the SCR system on containers, and the AdBlue and belly-tank alarm panel for generators 5 to 8, of which only the tanks for generator 5 were in use. The commissioning period must be reported in the annual report, and monitoring deadlines are aligned with final commissioning expected in Q1 2027.
sources.date_semantics: The report states the inspection date (11/08/2026) and the date issued (17/08/2026); the PDF's document properties give 28 September 2026, when it was evidently placed on the public register. The 17 August 2026 issue date is used as the publication date and the 11 August 2026 inspection as a dated first-hand regulator observation that the data-centre site was under construction and in commissioning. The Q1 2027 final-commissioning reference is a forecast and is not used as a stage. Names and initials of the officer and of company staff are not reproduced.

sources.title: Environment Agency Compliance Assessment Report YP3329SB/0605385: site inspection at LHR11/12, Chandos Road (permit EPR/YP3329SB, VDC LHR11 Limited), 11 August 2026, issued 17 August 2026
sources.publisher: Environment Agency (Public Registers Online, installations compliance documents)
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (Environment Agency conditional licence as stated in the register metadata)
sources.summary: Seven-page EPR Compliance Assessment Report for site 'LHR11/12', permit YP3329SB, operator/permit holder VDC LHR11 Limited: 'Site inspection - still under construction' on 11 August 2026 (14:30-15:00), carried out under CDM control after a liaison meeting at LHR21 with Vantage's environmental permitting manager, the LHR11 operations manager and a consultancy, 'for the commissioning of the site which was still under construction'. The officer notes that 'LHR 10 is near complete' and that the second separate building, LHR11, is yet to be started. The inspection covered the locked fuel fill point, interceptor alarm panel, double-skinned buried fuel tanks and their below-ground valve and pump chambers (an action to review pollution risk and leak alarms), the AdBlue fill point, multi-flue stacks, five engines per floor at ground level 1 with day tanks, and the SCR system; no breaches were scored (band A). The site has a dedicated load bank.
sources.date_semantics: The report states the inspection date (11/08/2026) and the date issued (17/08/2026); the PDF's document properties give 28 September 2026. The 17 August 2026 issue date is used as the publication date and the 11 August 2026 inspection as a dated first-hand regulator observation that the data-centre site was under construction, with one building near complete and a second not started. Names and initials of the officer and of company staff are not reproduced.

sources.title: Vantage Data Centers: 'Vantage Data Centers Announces Opening of Second London Campus with Landmark Public Art Installation' (11 September 2025)
sources.summary: Datelined 11 September 2025, Vantage announced that its second London data centre campus (LHR2), in Park Royal, 'will open at the end of September': a 194,000 sq ft (18,000 sq m) facility delivering 20 MW of IT capacity, a GBP 250 million investment, with a six-storey perforated public-art facade, BREEAM Excellent features and a planned connection to the local district heating network.
sources.date_semantics: Dated operator release outside the window. Its opening date is a stated target, not an observation, and is not used as a status; it is identity context for LHR2 (location, scale) only. Press contacts named in the release are not reproduced.
